Claude Desktop adapter (earlier setup)

The earlier Claude Desktop adapter profile (port 3467): how existing installations work, retiring it, and behavior shared with the direct setup.

About 19 min read · 11 sections

On this page
01 Account ownership and isolation 02 Prepare the desktop profile 03 Apply and run 04 One row per model, native thinking controls 05 Tools and subagents 06 Native Auto review 07 Context recovery for compatibility models 08 Empty completion recovery 09 Preserving Qwen output without tools 10 Verified coverage and limits 11 October 26 model mapping verification

For a new setup, use the Claude app guide. The gateway serves the Claude app itself; this page describes the separate adapter that earlier installations used, and behavior both setups share.

To move off the adapter, apply a direct profile. Nothing connects to the adapter afterwards. There is no retire command yet: the claude-adapter component (and any claude-inference tunnel) stays in state/service-plan.json until it is removed there, and then stops at the next idle service restart.

Claude Desktop rejects model IDs that name GPT or Qwen. The optional Claude adapter exposes stable opaque route IDs while retaining the actual provider and model in the picker label. Native Claude IDs still select the primary Claude account. A model is never redirected to another account after a failure.

Claude Desktop: truthful model labels
    → Claude-only loopback adapter
    → gateway Messages endpoint
        ├── Claude: primary subscription
        ├── Codex: first registered GPT account
        ├── Codex 2: second registered GPT account
        └── Local: configured Qwen server

This is an opt-in third-party inference profile. It does not add models to the first-party Claude subscription connection or modify the signed Claude app. The app keeps its third-party history under Claude-3p.

Account ownership and isolation

Give every GPT account its own gateway provider ID, model aliases, and scoped Sign in with ChatGPT registration. Register the intended email with gateway login PROVIDER --account-email EMAIL --config PATH. Native Codex authentication is not a gateway credential source. Copying a native login does not grant the gateway's required scopes.

When the existing Codex gateway must remain unchanged, keep Claude's separate gateway configuration, state directory and fixed loopback port. Configuration isolation does not require a separate macOS startup job: its adapter, private inference and SSH forwards belong to the existing signed app-owned service tree. Never install another LaunchAgent for them or reuse Codex's provider settings.

An existing scoped registration on the same inference host can be referenced through its existing absolute credential path. Do not create independent copies of rotating refresh credentials. For several Macs, one inference host and authenticated loopback SSH forwards avoid distributing provider credentials. Only the gateway client token and non-secret model ownership metadata belong on the other clients.

Repairing a Claude sign-in failure

Check the adapter's configured upstream and the inference host's private gateway configuration before reconnecting. A successful request to the shared gateway does not verify Claude Desktop's separate backend. Likewise, claude auth status over SSH can report no login when the macOS service can read it; verify an inference request through the app's actual adapter.

Native Desktop model IDs use the configured primary provider, which older deployments call claude. If that provider is intended to use a named Claude account, give it the same explicit authDirectory as that account. Renewing claude-primary cannot repair a legacy claude route that still reads the default login store. Verify the existing account identities before correcting the path, and preserve every model alias. The native review configuration's authDirectory must also select the intended review account.

Reconnect on the inference host, using its private configuration and the provider ID that owns the failing route:

gateway login PROVIDER --config /absolute/claude-gateway.json

The private inference process loads its configuration at startup. After a path correction, restart its owned component only when idle, within the existing app-owned service. Verify both a streamed Messages reply through the client's adapter and a native client tool round trip. Changing the client's token or recreating its profile does not renew the upstream subscription login.

Qwen remains the configured local or tailnet API provider. Use the existing endpoint and credential; selecting it does not turn it into a Claude model.

Prepare the desktop profile

The configuration library must already contain one selected profile named GateFox. Its credential helper and unrelated settings are preserved unless the configure command explicitly supplies the selected gateway helper.

gateway claude-desktop configure --gateway-config /absolute/claude-gateway.json

By default, this prepares candidate files under ~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p/alias-trial/candidate/. Review the profile and adapter configuration before applying. The source configuration is read-only; it may contain the gateway's provider configuration or only its model ownership metadata. Its authenticated live model catalog must agree with that metadata.

The default adapter port is 3467, the primary Claude provider ID is claude, and the default model is claude-fable-5-1. The command's help describes the overrides for other installations. It refuses collisions, missing primary routes, invalid catalogs, and an upstream endpoint that loops back to itself.

Native IDs map explicitly to the primary provider's public aliases. Secondary routes are derived from their public aliases, with real labelOverride values: claude-hg-route-<decimal hash> for a route without reasoning levels, and claude-opus-5[hg-route-<decimal hash>] for one with them, because the app only shows its native effort slider for a model ID it recognizes. Both forms retain the configured provider and account; neither adds a Claude family-tier field. The second borrows the claude-opus-5 ID shape for the control, which also makes the CLI assume a 1M context window; see the compaction limitation below. The label still names the real provider and model. Future accounts such as Claude 2 remain separate routes.

Apply and run

Finish Claude work and quit its GUI before applying:

gateway claude-desktop configure --gateway-config /absolute/claude-gateway.json --apply
gateway claude-desktop status --config /absolute/Claude-3p/desktop-adapter/config.json

The configure step stages the two files, creates private backups, and restores their exact previous bytes if replacement fails. It validates selected profile identity and path confinement before writing. The old standalone claude-desktop install command refuses to create another LaunchAgent. It does not unload an existing adapter or modify any profile.

For an existing standalone deployment, preview and stage consolidation through the main gateway configuration, not the Claude inference configuration:

gateway service claude-desktop --config /absolute/main-gateway.json
gateway service claude-desktop --on-restart --config /absolute/main-gateway.json

Staging leaves the live plan, jobs and listeners alone. The next primary service start revalidates the saved ownership receipts and adopts the Claude components only when every exact legacy registration is unloaded. A loaded adapter, inference process, or tunnel remains pending even when its sockets look idle: the pinned private runtime has no atomic drain. Changed or foreign jobs also remain pending. The signed app's Node runs the existing private runtime with its original arguments, working directory and configuration. Inference isolation, account ownership, models, permissions and client endpoints remain unchanged. Installation or staging is not proof of activation; check the live service tree and both authenticated loopback endpoints afterward.

During an approved maintenance window, an operator may stage one explicit interruption authorization:

gateway service claude-desktop --on-restart --force --config /absolute/main-gateway.json

--force is accepted only with this command. It is stored in that one pending receipt, still rechecks the exact signed app, plist hashes, argv and process identity, and can retire the owned loaded jobs despite active connections. The cutover may interrupt Claude work. Restaging without --force creates a normal safe receipt again; it is not a permanent service preference.

New component logs live under the main gateway state's services/ directory with private permissions. Existing launchd logs are retained unchanged rather than reused or chmodded. Recovery journals and original registrations stay in private service-backups storage.

For foreground diagnostics:

gateway claude-desktop serve --config /absolute/adapter-config.json

The adapter binds only 127.0.0.1, authenticates every endpoint, preserves query strings and tool content, and forwards status and streaming failures. It serves the model catalog and individual model detail required by the native picker. An optional private audit records only configured route identity and status, never prompts, tool arguments, headers, or credentials.

One row per model, native thinking controls

Recent clients can opt into native model metadata for their effort controls. The existing model-ID mapping remains the default.

An isolated, version-pinned native-picker experiment is available for developer testing. It is not part of the normal adapter or a deployment, and its native control transport still requires GUI verification.

Claude Desktop obtains its native effort controls from Anthropic's signed model catalog. The profile lists exactly one picker row per model and never lists effort or speed variants as separate rows. Recognized Claude IDs show the app's native effort control; the profile writes an accurate maxEffort for them (the model's highest supported effort, bounded by any cap already in the profile, so a user's lower cap is kept).

A secondary route that advertises reasoning levels is exposed as claude-opus-5[hg-route-<decimal>] so Claude Desktop shows its native slider for it: the app recognizes the ID before the bracket, and the app rejects any ID that names GPT or Qwen, so the suffix stays opaque. The row's labelOverride still names the real provider and model, the row adds no Claude family-tier field, and the slider is capped at the route's top supported effort. Only a cap already recorded under that bridge name counts as a user choice; the automatic maxEffort: "high" written on the old opaque row does not suppress the higher levels the route newly advertises. The adapter clamps a level the route does not support — to the highest supported level below it, or the lowest supported one — in the request and in the system-message history a tool continuation carries, and never adds an effort the client did not send or change thinking for these rows. The ID a saved chat used, claude-hg-route-<decimal>, stays in the adapter configuration as a hidden compatibility alias for the same route. A route with no reasoning levels is unchanged: it keeps the opaque claude-hg-route-<decimal> row, where the app offers no effort control.

These rows do not add Codex's Ultra agent orchestration to Claude Desktop, and Ultracode is not offered on the slider because the unmodified app never adds that stop to a third-party profile. Claude's CLI also treats a row with this ID shape as a 1M-token context. For a smaller upstream window, the client's normal proactive compaction threshold is too high. The gateway forwards a prompt is too long error that Claude can use for reactive recovery (see context overflow); the ID mapping alone does not prove that a long real conversation can compact successfully.

The adapter still accepts the deterministic explicit effort and speed aliases that earlier profiles listed, so chats saved against them keep working. They are backend-only: never written to the profile and never shown in the picker. Each carries an explicit effort and, where the transport honors it, a service tier (default for Standard). The generated count is bounded at 1000. Configuration fails with the required count when a catalog would exceed it and never evicts an alias, because a dropped alias would break a saved chat. Remove models or service tiers to get back under the bound.

Re-run claude-desktop configure to prepare the updated profile, then apply it after finishing Claude work and quitting its GUI. Existing base route IDs remain available for saved chats. An explicit alias's effort is authoritative for that alias, including tool continuations. An explicit effort variant enables adaptive thinking when the app sends its unknown-model disabled default. Existing adaptive display preferences are kept; fixed token budgets remain unsupported. Native auxiliary Auto reviews keep their original generation controls. The visible profile rows must fit Claude Desktop's 200-entry limit. Hidden aliases do not count. Configuration reports the required count and fails when the models alone would exceed the limit; it never silently drops a model.

Tools and subagents

The Claude harness executes tools and manages agents. The gateway continues to serve inference only. The adapter does not generate roles, choose worker models, change permissions, or silently substitute a model.

The Responses-backed GPT route can require optional tool properties to have a value. For opted-in codex-subscription and responses-api routes, the adapter represents optional non-nullable plain properties as nullable on the wire and removes only those introduced nulls from returned tool arguments. Required values, existing nullability, and explicit non-null choices are preserved. Reference and composition subtrees remain unchanged. This conversion is scoped to the Claude client and does not alter the existing Codex request path.

Native Auto review

Auto mode uses a second model to review proposed actions before the client executes them. The initial trial's review failed before inference: its disabled thinking and stop-sequence controls were unsupported by the subscription Messages translation. That failure was not a safety verdict.

An opt-in private inference entry point can serve native auxiliary reviews through a restricted, one-turn Claude CLI process:

gateway claude-desktop inference \
  --gateway-config /absolute/claude-gateway.json \
  --native-config /absolute/claude-native.json

Example native configuration:

{
  "command": "/absolute/path/to/claude",
  "models": {
    "claude/claude-sonnet-5": "claude-sonnet-5"
  },
  "timeoutMs": 60000,
  "maxConcurrent": 2,
  "maxRequestBytes": 262144,
  "contextProviders": ["qwen"],
  "emptyCompletionRecoveryProviders": ["qwen"]
}

Every native alias must belong to the same claude-subscription provider and native model in the gateway configuration. An optional authDirectory must match that provider. Use the existing signed-in CLI executable; --bare cannot use its OAuth or keychain login.

The listener keeps the private gateway's configured loopback port and serves ordinary requests through the original gateway on an ephemeral loopback port. Only explicitly configured, tool-free, nonstreaming Claude requests matching the observed native classifier control profiles use this transport. The native client normally omits request-class hints behind a custom endpoint; an absent hint is accepted, while an explicit conflicting hint stays on the ordinary backend. Original system, messages, and generation controls are preserved, and the native classifier protocol metadata is supplied to the Claude endpoint. No tool executes inside this process, and no permission verdict is invented. A response is returned only after a consistent completed native stream and successful terminal result. Refusals, truncation, cancellation, unsupported requests, and native failures remain failures.

The native request and child environment are bounded. Current Auto review requests can exceed 140 KiB even for a short task. The macOS bound accommodates these requests; a platform's smaller environment limit can still refuse one before spawning. The adapter never truncates a review transcript to make it fit.

Claude Code through the ordinary gateway reaches the same runner; see auto mode. This Desktop entry point stays separately configured, its backend does not use that general path, and it belongs only to the isolated Claude inference component inside the existing app-owned service. It does not share Codex's inference configuration or register a Codex client. Client cancellation also remains effective while asynchronous classifier selection is pending: a closed request cannot start fresh backend work when selection finishes. Ordinary streaming cancellation closes the owned upstream connection and releases the private request counters.

Context recovery for compatibility models

An unknown model ID makes Claude assume a 200K context window. This assumption can trigger early compaction as well as affect the meter. The current Desktop profile supports a 1M capability flag, not arbitrary numeric windows for each model. Advertising 1M for a smaller model is not a correction.

Claude Code documents CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1 for unknown aliases. Scoped to a Claude Desktop environment, it permits the provider to report its actual overflow and retains reactive and manual compaction. It does not correct the meter or provide an exact proactive threshold for every model. Do not set DISABLE_COMPACT as a substitute. The deployed backup clients retain conservative 200K enforcement; this override has not been enabled in their live Desktop environments.

The optional contextProviders list wraps only named Chat Completions providers inside this private service. It preserves the original endpoint, credential, and tailnet checks. A bounded, structured vLLM input-overflow error becomes the canonical context-overflow code before the unchanged provider adapter reads it. An excessive output-token request and unrelated HTTP 400 errors remain their original failures.

Empty completion recovery

The private inference configuration can opt selected Chat Completions providers into emptyCompletionRecoveryProviders. The entire list must name configured Chat Completions providers. The shared gateway factory and Responses ingress retain their existing behavior.

For an opted-in Messages request, a clean upstream completion with no answer text or tool fragments can trigger one additional request. Reasoning alone does not count as an answer. Recovery requires the exact configured upstream model, a normal stop, one completion marker, and clean stream closure within five seconds. Whitespace counts as visible text. Refusals, filtering, unknown semantic output, malformed streams, partial output, output limits, required or named tools, and nonempty stop-sequence lists are not eligible.

The retry preserves the same provider, account, model, serialized request, credentials, and generation controls. It has a separate 90-second deadline; the first request retains its existing caller timeout. A second empty completion returns an explicit incomplete-response error. This bounds recovery per gateway inference; Claude can independently retry a failed inference. The gateway never substitutes reasoning text for an answer.

The usage ledger retains spend from both attempts, including usage received before failure or cancellation. The Messages reply reports the final successful attempt's usage so repeated input is not mistaken for a doubled current context. Recovery telemetry contains route identity, outcome, timing, and numeric usage, without prompts or completion text.

Preserving Qwen output without tools

The private service can also opt Qwen into noToolsOutputRecoveryProviders, mapping its provider ID to an absolute tokenizer.json path:

{
  "contextProviders": ["qwen"],
  "emptyCompletionRecoveryProviders": ["qwen"],
  "noToolsOutputRecoveryProviders": {
    "qwen": "/absolute/Claude-3p/inference/tokenizers/qwen3.8-tokenizer.json"
  }
}

This addresses a vLLM no-tools parsing failure. Qwen can generate tool-shaped text after reasoning even when the request offers no tools. The configured upstream tool parser consumes that text, then removes the calls because tool use is disabled, leaving an empty successful reply.

For eligible requests, the private proxy requests raw token IDs as diagnostic metadata. It retains the same instructions, model, credentials, reasoning effort, and sampling controls. If the upstream supplies no visible text, a complete validated token sequence can recover the actual generated text after reasoning. That text remains ordinary text, including any unsolicited XML; it never becomes an executable tool call or an invented answer. Normal visible replies and requests offering tools retain their existing handling.

Recovery requires the final assistant prompt boundary, complete output ending in the configured EOS token, an unambiguous reasoning boundary, valid UTF-8, matching provider token counts, a normal stop, and clean stream closure. Invalid or incomplete evidence retains the existing empty-response retry and explicit failure. Added token metadata is removed before the normal provider and client see the response. Reasoning activity and usage continue streaming; only the final stop waits for validation. Buffering and closure waits are bounded.

The tokenizer is public data from nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, revision fc694b54fb0174e0913e6adf86691ef85a4ead47. Its exact SHA-256 is 0997f410c57a1f4e53b09e4be8f4a172d90edd9564368fb0847030937229b9f3. The service validates the asset before allocating listeners. It is stored in Claude's private configuration area and is not bundled with the gateway. The model card identifies the NVIDIA Open Model License and Qwen Community License 1.0 as governing terms. No tokenizer runtime dependency or model weights are added.

This policy preserves generated output; it does not guarantee that Qwen follows every instruction. It changes neither the shared Qwen workers nor the native Codex configuration or routing.

Verified coverage and limits

The initial macOS trial verified the rendered picker, real GPT and Qwen replies, switching models in one chat, exact file reads/writes, mixed-model native subagents, skills, MCP, background agents, resume, and GPT image input. Model identity was checked in child transcripts and route records rather than relying on the assistant's claim.

The October 19 private rollout passed real Auto-mode tasks through all three Macs' installed Desktop engines. Each GPT parent delegated a Qwen file reader and a second-account GPT writer, with exact output and four successful native Sonnet reviews. One earlier Qwen attempt skipped its assigned read and failed the validator; the successful retry does not qualify model reliability for every task. These checks used the native engine.

A separate rendered Desktop task on macbook-server also passed in Auto mode: the default Fable parent delegated only to the assigned Qwen reader and second-account GPT writer. Retained child transcripts confirm their models, tools, and file paths, and the output matches the source byte for byte. No session permission override was added. This GUI task used the native-review runtime before the subsequent cancellation-only fix; the fixed package passed its own complete native cancellation chain and a live Fable request.

  • Keep Manual permissions on another installation until its native review transport passes a real Auto-mode task. Manual remains a fallback, and the deployed GUI's saved permission choice remains unchanged.
  • Routes without reasoning levels keep opaque aliases and Claude's generic 200K context estimate. Mapped reasoning routes expose the native effort control but inherit a 1M client estimate. Neither estimate establishes the provider's true limit; see the compaction limitation above.
  • Native Claude mobile Remote Control excludes custom gateways and proxies. Desktop aliases do not remove that restriction.
  • Provider capabilities still apply. A text-only Qwen route does not accept images, and switching providers replays the conversation.
  • Short connectivity proofs do not qualify long-session compaction or every possible MCP JSON schema.

October 26 model mapping verification

Claude Desktop 3.6556.2 on the MacBook displayed its own Effort submenu on a mapped Codex · GPT-6.1-Sol row: Low, Medium, High, Extra, and Max. This build uses a submenu rather than the slider seen in the older trial. The cropped capture shows that native control and the truthful GPT label together. The deployment preserved the existing 25 visible rows; 21 received mapped reasoning controls. The adapter kept its old IDs for saved chats. This deployment updated the profile and the private adapter under the existing gateway service.

A separate native CLI 2.1.299 process used a private home, a local synthetic backend, and the exact deployed adapter code. Its bracketed model ID survived the CLI and mapped to the expected backend ID; the completed turn carried xhigh. Explicit native control requests also reported applied Ultracode active and available. The sanitized CLI receipt records those flags and the backend effort, without prompts or credentials. That protocol check does not add an Ultracode item to the Desktop menu or verify real-provider workflow fan-out.

Claude.app retained the same archive SHA-256 and passed strict deep signature verification after installation. No app patch or re-signing was performed. The MacBook's gateway rollout and direct-tool canary reported ready; health reported ok. A real provider turn selected through the GUI and long-session compaction remain unverified.

Offline native-engine fixtures exercise overflow, reactive compaction, and a smaller retry through the actual GPT and Qwen provider adapters. A live Qwen overflow also produces the recognized context error through the private frontend. These checks do not establish a larger Desktop context meter or qualify long-running live compaction.

A bounded live Qwen manual-compaction task also passed: the native engine emitted a real compact boundary and retained a seeded fact before and after a separate resume process. The manual phase took about 63 seconds. Its initial seed replies contained no assistant text and were not treated as substantive completions. This qualifies that bounded manual workflow, not automatic compaction at a large live context window.

Separate live checks on both registered GPT accounts processed about 193K provider input tokens with conservative 200K client enforcement. The native engine compacted automatically and retained a seeded fact after compaction and after a separate resume process. The later prompts did not reinsert the fact. These bounded synthetic-text checks do not qualify multi-hour workloads.

A fresh Qwen automatic-compaction check stopped before its large-input phase: two HTTP 200/end-turn responses contained no assistant content, followed by an empty native success result. Retain that failed sample; it establishes a blank reply, not an automatic-compaction failure. An unchanged repeat then passed at 193,210 provider input tokens, including native automatic compaction and fact recall before and after restart, after trimming surrounding whitespace. The repeat does not qualify first-attempt reliability. An isolated content-path probe also confirmed that all visible upstream answer text reached the native client unchanged; its strict comparison failed only because the correct marker had surrounding whitespace.

An isolated native-engine cancellation proof uses the deployed adapter, inference frontend, gateway, provider, and context proxy with a controlled HTTP upstream. Interrupting before headers and after a content delta closes the upstream socket before fixture cleanup, returns all owned components to idle, and permits a subsequent native request. This does not inspect remote providers' internal generation jobs.

Run npm run build, npm run check, and npm test. The adapter's loopback fixtures also run separately with npm run test:claude-desktop. Packaging includes all three Claude runtime modules; no Python runtime is required.
